# Decoder fixtures

These tiny 32×24 solid-blue images were generated for Paint Studio's regression tests. They contain no user photos or third-party artwork.

TIFF, PSD, AVIF, JPEG XL and JPEG 2000 were independently encoded with the previous application's ImageMagick WASM 0.0.44. The Rust tests decode them and check dimensions and pixel colors. This verifies interoperability rather than only asking a decoder to read its own output.

HEIC was encoded from the same solid-blue PNG with libheif/heif-enc 1.17.6 and x265, in lossless mode.

The uncompressed Bayer DNG `sensor.dng` is generated by `tests/fixtures/make-dng.py` with an original constant sensor pattern, identity color matrix and DNG metadata. It tests the real Rawler development path.

`generate-import-fixtures.py` creates original red/blue BMP and ICO fixtures with
RGB24, indexed Info/Core palettes, external 16-bit bitmasks and embedded V4/V5
bitmasks. Tests mutate their pixel offsets independently. ICO exercises the DIB
path without a BMP file header.

`webp-exif-overflow.webp` is the 64-byte synthetic EXIF-length reproducer from
[image #3135](https://github.com/image-rs/image/pull/3135), also recorded in the
16 November investigation. Changing bytes 56–59 to little-endian 4 creates its
valid 1×1 control. Native regression tests refuse allocations above 320 MB before
allocating, so reverting the fix fails safely rather than reserving gigabytes.
